Marissa / Daria — quick update from triage (initial observations):

What we see:
- Around 22:12–22:18 UTC there were repeated failed DNS resolutions originating from our regional resolvers for the Blue Harbor customer hostname; cache miss volume spiked 12x.
- Concurrently, we observed a partial flap on the VPC peering session between our us-east-1 peering fabric and Blue Harbor’s peering (BGP withdraws and re-advertisements).
- Firewall logs (excerpt attached) show a large number of TCP connections reset/timeout when the flows hit the proxy layer (likely caused by SNAT port exhaustion on the proxy -> backend path under peak concurrent connections).

Likely root contributors (hypothesis):
1) Transient BGP instability caused route churn so some requests were hitting an alternate egress that had stale DNS cache behavior.
2) Resolver timeouts amplified the tail latency and forced retries.
3) On the proxy hop, per-tenant SNAT ports were exhausted causing resets/504s for long-lived requests.

Immediate mitigations we’re pushing (now):
- Enable alternate peering path for Blue Harbor prefix to avoid the flapping peer (workaround activated at 23:00 UTC).
- Increase SNAT pool size for the affected proxy cluster and apply a short TTL override on the resolver to reduce cache churn (TTL set to 30s temporarily).
- We’ve opened a ticket with the colo provider for the BGP instability and requested an expedited SR (SR-928324).

Planned next steps (30–120m):
- Run a controlled canary to route a small percentage of BH traffic through the alternate peering and monitor 5xx and p95.
- Coordinate a coordinated flush/update of resolver caches across the affected fabric.
- If SNAT resizing and canary succeed, schedule a permanent SNAT pool increase and review peering health checks.

Attachments: fw-logs-snip-20261206.txt (firewall resets), peering-bgp-dump-20261206.log

I’ll post metrics in 15 minutes.

— Rishi
